entities.name: Sri Vijaya Rajasinha of Kandy
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Sri Vijaya Rajasinha of Kandy (1747-08-11) was the King of Kandy from 1747 to 1747, succeeding his brother-in-law Vira Narendra Sinha. He was the second ruler of the Madurai Nayak Dynasty and a member of the royal family of Kandy, known for his involvement in the politics and culture of the court and society at large.

Born in Kandy, Sri Lanka, and raised in the city's royal court, Rajasinha was familiar with the politics and culture of the region, including those of his Telugu kinfolk. His reign was marked by an ongoing struggle for power and control with neighboring kingdoms.

Rajasinha's legacy is largely overshadowed by that of his brother-in-law Vira Narendra Sinha, who played a more significant role in the history of Kandy. Nevertheless, Rajasinha's reign marked an important period in the history of the Madurai Nayak Dynasty and the kingdom of Kandy.

The 'Battle of Kandy', fought during Rajasinha's reign, resulted in the kingdom's defeat and subsequent capture by the British East India Company in 1815. The British then annexed the kingdom, marking the end of the Madurai Nayak Dynasty.
